subject: Low-latency pilot: priority GPU bucket request & product impact
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Low-latency pilot: priority GPU bucket request & product impact

Hi team,

EdgeHealth (external) reached out with a time-sensitive pilot: they want to run a patient-facing inference flow that requires 30–50ms tail latency (p50/p95), ~120 concurrent sessions at peak, ~250k tokens/day for a two-week pilot. They plan to use an LLaMA-derivative (7B) with int8 quant and small context windows, but latency sensitivity is strict.

Ask: can we carve a short-term priority bucket (dedicated GPUs, isolated pool) and grant an autoscale policy exception so we don't fall back to cheaper model variants during the pilot? Specifics:
- Window: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-16 (14 days)
- Rough compute: equivalent of 8 A100 80GB nodes (continuous during business hours, burst evenings)
- Autoscale exception: allow steady-state pool above default hard cap (temporary override)
- SLO: p95 < 120ms, target p50 < 40ms

Product/roadmap note: this pilot maps to an upcoming latency-optimization epic in Nov. If we approve an exception, we should capture telemetry and cost to inform the prioritization tradeoffs (batching vs dedicated slices).

I attached a short pilot_requirement_matrix.xlsx with EdgeHealth's numbers. Can Kimberly and Marcus weigh in on feasibility and tradeoffs? Laura — ops — can you sketch what operational runbook/backfill would look like if we approve?

Thanks,
Mateo
Staff Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Low-latency pilot: priority GPU bucket request & product impact

Thanks Mateo — good summary. A couple of clarifying Qs before we commit:

1) Start/length: is 11/2 fixed? EdgeHealth asks for a two-week window but is flexible by a few days. We need the exact runway to check against other reservations.
2) Model variant: can the customer accept a quantized 4-bit/8-bit variant if it materially reduces cost but still meets latency? If they insist on FP16 we may need more capacity.
3) Telemetry: I want the pilot to ship with a minimal eval suite so we can capture quality/regression risk. Can we force a canary model ID and a fixed prompt set?

Tradeoffs from product POV: approving a carveout is fine for proving the feature, but we should record expected downstream work: (a) integrating dedicated-bucket routing into SDKs, (b) documenting autoscale-exceptions for customers. If Marcus says it's feasible capacity-wise, I'm ok gating on a clear go/no-go 72hrs before start.

Assigning: Mateo please confirm final dates with EdgeHealth. Marcus — can you provide a short feasibility matrix (capacity + cost delta) by EOD tomorrow? Laura — preliminary runbook would be great.

-Kimberly
Senior PM, Dedicated Products
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Low-latency pilot: priority GPU bucket request & product impact

Quick feasibility note after an initial capacity check:

- Current available headroom (US-west): equivalent of ~12 A100 nodes for the 11/02–11/16 window, but ~40% of that is already earmarked for scheduled pilots (commitments). We can carve 8 A100-equivalent nodes for the requested window but with these constraints:
  * We will need an autoscale exception to allow the priority bucket to exceed the normal per-customer cap.
  * Nightly batch jobs running in that cluster must be shifted or throttled — ops will need to coordinate backfill.
  * If EdgeHealth requires FP16 with larger context it could push required capacity to ~12 nodes.

Proposal:
- Grant 8-node carveout for the 14-day window with the autoscale exception limited to business hours (08:00–20:00 PST). Nighttime runs (20:00–08:00) will be scheduled on preemptible capacity.
- Require a go/no-go confirmation 72 hours before the start date. If we get to T-48hrs with no confirmation, the carveout will be reclaimed.

I've sketched a runbook and cost delta in carveout_runbook.md attached. High-level cost impact is ~+$14k for the two weeks (net of expected backfill recovery). If Kimberly and Laura are OK with the operational tradeoffs I'll start the reservations paperwork and the autoscale policy override ticket.

- Marcus
Infra Lead, Serving Runtime
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@edgehealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Low-latency pilot: priority GPU bucket request & product impact

Alex — looping you in with the internal folks and proposed plan.

Summary for EdgeHealth:
- Redwood can provision an 8-node dedicated slice (A100-equivalent) for 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-16, with an autoscale exception limited to business hours (08:00–20:00 PST). Nighttime workloads will run on preemptible capacity.
- Expected cost uplift for Redwood during the window is roughly $14k; procurement/contract implications below.
- We need confirmation from EdgeHealth to lock the carveout by 2026-10-30 (this is the 72hr + buffer go/no-go).

Questions for you: can you confirm whether EdgeHealth can: (a) accept a quantized int8 model (recommended) or need FP16; (b) sign the short pilot addendum (I attached the pilot_requirement_matrix.xlsx and will send a DocuSign for the carveout addendum once we get mutual agreement).

Next steps: if you confirm model variant and sign the addendum, Marcus will file the autoscale-exception and Laura will publish the operational runbook.

Best,
Mateo
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@edgehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Low-latency pilot: priority GPU bucket request & product impact

Thanks all — ops can support the proposed plan with these operational controls:

- Runbook: priority-bucket-runbook v1 is published to Drive (https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/edgehealth-pilot-specs). It includes escalation steps, monitoring dashboards (token-level latency charts), and a rollback play (immediate rollback to standard routing + canary model).
- Backfill: we will throttle nightly batch jobs and requeue to preemptible lanes; estimated customer-facing impact minimal.
- Cost/charge: we will log incremental infra costs against deal HD-4729; finance will invoice pilot uplift per the addendum.

Confirming: autoscale exception ticket will be opened once we receive EdgeHealth sign-off on model variant and DocuSign addendum. Go/no-go cutoff: 2026-10-30 23:59 PDT.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
Operational runbook: priority-bucket-runbook v1 (see Drive)
